title: Strobed prefetch attention throughput playbook
summary: Working notes for an experiment series evaluating a strobing prefetch strategy for attention kernels. Focus is on mixed-sequence workloads where conventional continuous prefetch or coarse-grain batching causes throughput cliffs or tail latency spikes. Primary goals: (1) measure throughput uplift, (2) identify microstutter modes, (3) collect artifacts for a potential fused-op fallback path.
body:
Context:
- Multiple customer workloads show intermittent tail latency and throughput cliffs when mixing short and long sequences in a single worker queue. Current prefetch approach warms KV cache aggressively per-request which increases contention and memory bandwidth pressure for flash/paged-backed kernels.
- Hypothesis: a strobed prefetch schedule (periodic, aligned to wavefronts and batch coalescing windows) reduces noisy prefetch interactions while preserving hit rate in common prefix-heavy workloads.

Hypotheses and expected signals:
- Hypothesis A: Strobing at 8-16 microsecond granularity will reduce kernel launch jitter induced by asynchronous DMA storms. Signal: reduced variance in inter-token time and fewer sub-10ms tail spikes.
- Hypothesis B: Grouped prefetch (aligning prefetch windows to coalesced batch boundaries) will improve small-batch GPU utilization without increasing per-request latency for short sequences. Signal: higher throughput measured in tokens/sec for mixed workload ratio (70% short, 30% long).
- Hypothesis C: A lightweight abort-and-fallback for fused ops when prefetch contention detected will trade a small median latency increase for more stable p95/p99. Signal: p99 downshift despite small median cost.

Experiment design — harness and controls:
- Hardware: A100-40GB (nvlink disabled) and H100-80GB (single GPU VPC sim)
- Runtime: current mainline branch with toggles for prefetch_mode={continuous, strobed, disabled} and fusion_fallback={on,off}
- Workloads (synthetic):
  - mix-A: 70% seq=32, 20% seq=256, 10% seq=1024 (prefix-heavy chat-like)
  - mix-B: uniform 1..1024 (worst-case variability)
  - production-replay: sanitized sample from customer X (mixed bursts)
- Metrics captured: per-token latency histogram (µs), kernel launch timestamps, PCIe DMA counters, GPU SM occupancy, L2/HBM bandwidth, KV cache hit ratio, batch composition window sizes, eviction counts.
- Runs: 20 warmup iterations + 200 measurement iterations per condition. Randomize seed and interleave runs across hardware to control for thermal drift.

Prefetch strobed policy variants:
- strobed-fixed-8us, strobed-fixed-16us, strobed-adaptive (feedback loop based on recent eviction rate), group-aligned (emit prefetch at batch-coalesce boundaries only)

Preliminary results summary (sanitized):
- mix-A on A100: strobed-fixed-8us increased sustained tokens/sec by ~9% vs continuous prefetch; p99 reduced by ~18%. Median latency unchanged (<2% delta).
- mix-B on H100: strobed-adaptive reduced number of sub-5ms microstutters from ~42 events/min to ~7 events/min, but introduced slightly higher variance in batch sizes which transiently lowered peak throughput by ~3%.
- Fusion fallback: enabling fallback eliminated large p99 tails attributable to a pathological fused-op kernel that had 0.2% catastrophic slow calls under certain alignment patterns. Overall cost: median +1.6% latency.

Anomalies observed / debugging notes:
- Occasional long DMA stalls traced to NVML-reported page faults when HBM pressure crossed a threshold. Repro steps: replay mix-B with synthetic noise (50% additional background embedding lookups).
- A rare sequence alignment case where strobed prefetch missed a hot prefix and caused a cache miss cascade; seen only when long sequences immediately follow many short sequences (<500ms window). Hypothesis: adaptive policy needs a per-request priority bump on detected recent-miss patterns.
- SM occupancy telemetry shows lower utilization spikes right after a strobed window during which a large batch landed; indicates scheduling ripple. Consider inserting a micro-coalescer that rotates small batches across warps to smooth.

Measurement pitfalls to watch for:
- Clock sync between userland timestamps and GPU kernel timestamps. We added cross-correlation anchor events but still see ~100us jitter in some traces.
- PCIe counters have low sampling resolution on the instance images used earlier; preferring perf counters from vendor library for final runs.
- Ensure randomization of input order; deterministic sequences hide burst interaction patterns.

Suggested next steps and action items:
- Short term (this sprint):
  - (Maya) land strobed-prefetch small PR with config toggle and unit tests for timing jitter emulation (linear ISSUE-642).
  - (Ethan) add adaptive policy prototype that increases prefetch window after observed eviction spikes; add telemetry to flag missed-prefetch cascades.
  - (Rina) run longer 12-hour soak on H100 with mix-B + background embedding noise to surface low-frequency faults.
- Mid term:
  - Evaluate micro-coalescer prototype to smooth post-strobe warping effects.
  - Add a fused-op watchdog that measures per-kernel latency tail and triggers safe fallback when >0.05% slow calls observed.
- Metrics to report to product and SRE:
  - tokens/sec change per workload, delta p95/p99, background eviction rate, percentage of runs with >3 microstutters/min.

Open questions and discussion points:
- What is the acceptable median-to-tail tradeoff for enterprise SLAs (product input needed)?
- Should strobed prefetch be enabled by default for Dedicated customers vs host API?
- How to expose policy knobs in Console without overwhelming customers? (propose: presets: conservative, balanced, aggressive)

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Consider a hybrid \"tagged prefetch\" where requests can mark a prefix as latency-sensitive; strobed system then preferentially warms those prefixes outside of bulk windows. Useful for real-time assistants.
- Could probe if NVLINK peer copies can be scheduled to hide DMA storms when multi-GPU colocations are present.

Appendix (artifacts):
- Jenkins job IDs: perf-run-2024-10-22-14:00 (A100), perf-run-2024-10-28-03:30 (H100 soak)
- Files: /perftools/strobes/mixA-a100-run1.log, /perftools/strobes/h100-soak-20241028.tar.gz (stored in internal bucket)
notes: Informal lab book style. This is an experimental playbook intended for engineers on the serving-runtime team. Keep rough debugging traces and provisional conclusions here before migrating relevant findings to a formal ops runbook or RFC.
